Expectation1: Be friendly and polite in daily interactions
Situation1: Having just moved in, they prepare a small cake to share with nearby neighbors when they happen to meet.
Expectation2: Challenge unfair systems and influence policy change
Situation2: They gather recurring cases of unfair treatment and bring them to discussions with community leaders or officials.
Story: I had just moved into the building, and with a small cake in hand, I rehearsed my introduction for the neighbors I’d soon meet. I wanted to be friendly, to show I cared about the people living around me. As I walked down the hall, I saw Mrs. Lee, who smiled warmly and invited me in for tea. We chatted, and she mentioned how the landlord often ignored maintenance requests from tenants who didn’t speak English well. My advocate instincts kicked in—I’d already heard similar stories from others and was preparing to bring these issues to the next community meeting. But as a neighbor, I was supposed to be polite, to build trust, not to make anyone uncomfortable. If I brought up these problems too forcefully, would I seem confrontational? Would I lose the chance to connect with people like Mrs. Lee? The cake felt heavier in my hands as I wondered how to balance being a good neighbor with my drive to challenge the unfairness I saw.
